name: What is the best pool finish for hard water areas in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Which resurfacing material handles hard water, mineral staining, and scale best in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: Which resurfacing material handles hard water, mineral staining, and scale best in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Los Angeles-area pools, hard water is a major factor because mineral scale can shorten the life of lighter, softer finishes. Quartz and pebble aggregate surfaces generally perform better than basic plaster because they are harder, denser, and less likely to etch or stain. Quartz often gives a smoother feel and cleaner appearance, while pebble tends to be the most durable and forgiving for long-term use. Standard plaster is usually the lowest-cost option, but it is more vulnerable to scale, mottling, and visible wear if water chemistry is not maintained closely. Homeowners should also think about maintenance: a premium finish can still look bad if pH, calcium hardness, and alkalinity are neglected. For a decision in Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, or similar markets, the best answer is usually a finish that balances durability with the level of maintenance the homeowner is actually willing to do. Ask for sample boards and confirm the startup and care requirements before choosing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Quartz and pebble finishes usually resist staining and scale better than standard white plaster because they are denser and more durable. In hard-water areas, the best choice depends on budget, texture preference, and maintenance habits. Even premium finishes still need balanced water chemistry to avoid calcium buildup and discoloration.
